events.body:

[F2 F3 F5 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D2: Duration is irrelevant when the position requirement fails: the 4 min 0 s stationary period in F3 was spent 181 m from the pickup, and NS-1 requires (ii) position and (iii) duration together, so a long wait at the wrong spot still sends the case to NS-2. [F3 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]

→ D5: The amount charged is not in dispute — $6.61 is the published figure (F8, F9) — but NS-2 refunds the full $6.61 precisely when NS-1's conditions fail, so the exact fee being charged is why the refund is owed. [F8 F9] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D6: I agree no traffic factor is in play and none blocks the driver from reaching the pin; fair weather and no incidents (F14, F15, F16) mean the only reason he stopped 181 m short was his own choice (F3). [F3 F14 F15 F16] [RD-4]
→ D7: Profile facts may never decide the case; the outcome turns on the system record of the driver's position (F3, F6), not on the rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes or the driver's 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F17, F18). [F3 F6 F17 F18] [RD-6]

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The cancellation was initiated by the driver [F4], so NS-0 routes the rider's no-show fee challenge exclusively through NS-1/NS-2 [RD-NS-0][RD-NS-2]; the $6.61 fee stands only if all three NS-1 limbs hold, otherwise NS-2 mandates a full refund.

Limb (i) — the "I'm Here" precondition — is satisfied on the system record: the timeline logs the driver's arrival at 14:06:40 and a tap at 14:07:40 [F6], and the execution trace settles this element as passed. The conflicting null value in the separate timeline slice [F5][F7] is a record inconsistency the trace has already resolved against; where a timeline slice is internally inconsistent, I follow the slice that agrees with the distance evidence (181 m at the tap, 60 m closest approach) [F1][F6].

Limb (ii) — position at the moment of the tap — is also settled as passed: the driver was 181 m from the pin when he tapped, having come as close as 60 m [F1][F6]. NS-1(ii) requires only that GPS place the driver at the pick-up location, and Ryde publishes no metre figure for that test (policy gap G2); accordingly the 200 m radius is a data-layer parameter, not a clause whose tightening the rider can demand, and I cannot convert it into a pass/fail of its own. The driver's position was inside the range recorded by the platform at the moment of, and throughout, the wait [F2][F6].

Limb (iii) — duration — is satisfied: the driver held inside 200 m cumulatively for 4 min 40 s, and 3 min 40 s of that was after the tap [F6][F2], well over the 3:01 threshold; he was stationary 181 m out for the final 4 min 0 s until cancelling at 14:11:20 [F3][F4]. All three limbs hold, so NS-1 applies and the passenger cancellation fee is validly charged [RD-NS-1]; NS-2, which the rider invokes, is the clause for the case where a limb fails [RD-NS-2] and is therefore inapplicable. The fee amount charged is the published figure with no surge component [F8][F9], so no FARE-1 add-on issue arises [RD-FARE-1].

No traffic or weather factor is in play and none is needed: there are no speed-band or incident records and the weather was fair [F14][F15][F16], so RD-4 is not engaged either to exempt or excuse anything [RD-RD-4]. The profile records are not used to decide the fee — the rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes and the driver's 1 dispute with 0 upheld are relevant only to an ancillary account action, and neither RD-6 nor NS-2's flag limb is triggered here [F17][F18][RD-RD-6]. ✓ NS-1 (ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the tap [case] 181 m from pickup when tapped (closest approach overall 60 m) (F6, F1)
✓ NS-1 (iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling [case] 220 s continuously inside the radius after the tap (F6)

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled while claiming the rider was a no-show, so the $6.61 fee can only stand if NS-1 is fully satisfied; NS-0 routes this driver-cancellation no-show claim through NS-1/NS-2.
The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 181 m from the pickup point, which the GPS record shows is his position at that moment — he was not at the pick-up location (no show of arrival at the pin).

The driver's closest approach to the pickup was 60 m at 14:07:00 but he then moved back and sat stationary 181 m away from 14:07:20 until the 14:11:20 cancellation, so the arrival position did not satisfy the proximity requirement at the moment he claimed arrival.
The cancellation fee of $6.61 must be fully refunded because not all of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) were fulfilled: the driver was outside the acceptable pick-up range when he pressed "I'm Here".

The rider was waiting at the entrance the driver was told to meet and messaged at 14:09 "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you", while the driver merely said he was on the side road — the rider was ready and reachable; no fare is owed.

The driver's account has 1 dispute with 0 upheld in 90 days over 1,282 trips, so there is no prior pattern of upheld no-show claims by this driver; the rider's own history does not alter the GPS-based result.

The route and traffic records show no incidents or congestion that could explain the driver stopping 181 m short (no speed bands, no incidents, fair weather), so there was no operational reason for the driver not to reach the pin.

weaknesses: The driver's statement (F13) claims he was 'parked at the pickup, a short walk from the entrance' and waited more than 3 minutes; and the timeline shows the rider was within 200 m of the pickup for 4 min 40 s and the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap (F2, F5, F6), so the driver will argue he did wait and that the rider failed to walk over.

NS-1's proximity requirement is an unpublished radius (policy gap G2), so the driver can argue 181 m still counts as 'at the pick-up location according to GPS data'; the 200 m figure is a data-layer parameter, not a policy number the rider can cite.

claims.assertion: The system recorded the driver's arrival at the pickup within range: GPS shows him first within 200 m of the pin at 14:06:40 and continuously inside 200 m for a cumulative 4 min 40 s before cancellation, so the 'I'm Here' / at-pickup condition is satisfied on the system record.

The driver waited longer than the 3-minute threshold while at the pickup: he was stationary at 181 m from the pickup for 4 min 0 s (14:07:20-14:11:20) and the platform records cancellation 4 min 40 s after the recorded arrival, both exceeding 3:01.

The driver's closest approach to the pin was 60 m at 14:07:00 and he held position ~181 m away on a side road, so the rider's complaint that he 'was not at the entrance' reflects the pin point, not the driver's absence from the pickup locality.

The driver announced his presence and position and warned the rider before cancelling ('I'm here … at the side road' at 14:07; 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' at 14:11), so the cancellation followed, rather than substituted for, the required waiting procedure.
The $6.61 cancellation fee on record and the absence of any surge multiplier mean the fee charged is exactly the published Ryde cancellation amount and contains no inflated or extra component.

No traffic or weather factor is needed to justify the driver's position, and none contradicts it: the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain and no incidents or speed-band records affect the pickup window, so there is no system evidence that the pickup point was unreachable.

The rider has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days, both categorised no-show, while the driver has 0 upheld disputes across 1282 trips in 90 days — the pattern of the rider not being found at the pin is not attributable to this driver.

weaknesses: The timeline slice is internally inconsistent: F6 says the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 14:07:40 while 181 m from the pickup, but F7 says driver_pressed_here_at is null. NS-1(i) requires the tap, and on F7 the rider will argue the 'I'm Here' precondition was never met, which on its own would move the case to NS-2 (full refund of $6.61).

The rider will rely on F3 and F1: the driver was stationary 181 m away and only ever came within 60 m of the pin, so on the rider's reading he was never 'at the pick-up location' — and F11 ('I'm at the entrance, I don't see you') supports that the rider was present and searching.

NS-2's flag_account limb is a live risk: if the judge accepts that the driver pressed 'I'm Here' (F6) while GPS placed him outside the pickup range at that moment (181 m, F3), Ryde treats abuse of the arrival button as a fraud category and may add an account flag rather than deny the fee.
The driver's own written statement (F13) is self-serving and, per the record hierarchy, cannot carry the case where GPS/timeline facts cut against it; the case therefore turns on F2/F5/F3 alone.

points.response: D1 concedes the case against itself: NS-1 requires the driver to be at the pick-up location, and the timeline shows the only tap recorded was made 181 m from the pin while he then held that 181 m position (F3, F6); being 'within 200 m' is the data-layer radius, not a policy criterion, so F2/F5 cannot establish NS-1(ii).

Duration is irrelevant when the position requirement fails: the 4 min 0 s stationary period in F3 was spent 181 m from the pickup, and NS-1 requires (ii) position and (iii) duration together, so a long wait at the wrong spot still sends the case to NS-2.

A 60 m closest approach at 14:07:00 followed by withdrawal to 181 m until cancellation (F1, F3) is not 'at the pick-up location' under NS-1(ii), and the rider's own message 'I'm at the entrance, I don't see you' (F11) confirms the rider was at the pin while the driver was on a side road (F10).

Announcing a location does not satisfy NS-1; the driver's messages place him on a side road, not the pick-up point (F10, F12), and no agreement to relocate the meeting point appears in the chat, so the arrival precondition remains unmet.

The amount charged is not in dispute — $6.61 is the published figure (F8, F9) — but NS-2 refunds the full $6.61 precisely when NS-1's conditions fail, so the exact fee being charged is why the refund is owed.

I agree no traffic factor is in play and none blocks the driver from reaching the pin; fair weather and no incidents (F14, F15, F16) mean the only reason he stopped 181 m short was his own choice (F3).

Profile facts may never decide the case; the outcome turns on the system record of the driver's position (F3, F6), not on the rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes or the driver's 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F17, F18).

Accepted as the correct routing — the fee can stand only through NS-1 — but the same clause's three conditions are met on the system records, not defeated by them: F2 shows the driver inside 200 m from 14:06:40 with 4 min 40 s accumulated inside range, and F5 records cancellation 4 min 40 s after the recorded arrival.

The rider reads the 200 m figure as a policy radius, but it is a data-layer parameter, not a clause; on the record the driver was within 200 m of the pin for the whole relevant window (F2) and his closest approach was 60 m (F1), and no clause imposes a tighter pin-exact requirement.

Sitting 181 m from the pin for 4 min 0 s (F3) still places the driver within the pickup range for the full wait period per F2, and the timeline records him arriving at 14:06:40 and cancelling only 4 min 40 s later (F5), so the proximity and duration conditions are satisfied on the system record rather than broken by it.

NS-2 applies only if a NS-1 limb fails; limbs (ii) and (iii) are affirmatively proved by F2 (4 min 40 s within 200 m) and F5 (cancelled 4 min 40 s after recorded arrival), and limb (i) is recorded at F6 (tap at 14:07:40, 3 min 40 s of range subsequently held), so no full refund arises.

The rider's own messages show she was told exactly where the driver was waiting and did not come to him: F10 states 'at the side road' at 14:07, F11 answers only that she could not see him, and F12 records the driver cancelling after the wait had already elapsed, which is NS-1 conduct, not NS-2 conduct.

The parties' profile records do not decide the fee either way — F17 and F18 are relevant only to an ancillary account action and never to the main finding, so the rider gains nothing from the driver's clean history and the rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) is a pattern point, not a substitute for the GPS record.

RD-4 governs reroute justification and is not a NS-1 condition; absence of congestion (F14, F15) with fair weather (F16) simply means the driver had no reason to abandon the pickup, and indeed he did not — he held position 181 m away inside the pickup range for 4 min 0 s (F3) until the fee-eligible cancellation.

Conceded in part for candour, not on the merits: the timeline slice conflicts — F6 records a tap at 14:07:40 while 181 m out, F7 records driver_pressed_here_at as null — so limb (i) for the driver rests on F6 alone, while limbs (ii) and (iii) remain independently proved by F2 and F5.
